title: Article on Termination After Occupancy and Changes of Apartment, Entrance Fee Agreement
content:
**Article 1. Notice by the resident.** After occupancy the resident terminates the Entrance Fee Agreement only by a signed written notice; the agreement terminates on the notice date plus the plan's termination notice period in calendar days. The notice must be signed by the resident or by a representative whose authority on the customer profile is a financial power of attorney, a durable power of attorney or a guardianship.

**Article 2. Counting the notice period.** A termination after notice may be recorded only once the plan's termination notice period has passed since the notice was signed. The notice period is counted in calendar days from the notice date, the notice date being day 0, and the agreement terminates on the day the count reaches the plan's termination notice period. The notice date is the one recorded on the agreement.

**Article 3. Withdrawal.** A notice may be withdrawn at any time before the termination date, and the agreement then continues as if no notice had been given. A withdrawal must be signed in the same way as a notice.

**Article 4. Death.** Where the plan ends the agreement on death without a notice period, the agreement terminates on the date of death of the last resident, evidenced only by the date of death on the customer profile, and the refund is payable to the estate. When one of two residents dies the agreement continues for the survivor.

**Article 5. Care benefit and moves to care.** The plan's contract type decides the care benefit: a fee-for-service plan discounts future care, and a lifecare plan covers care level fees almost entirely through its larger discounts. A move to Larkspur assisted living or memory care on the campus is not a termination where the plan keeps the agreement in force on such a move; it changes no refund term and brings the plan's care fee discount and rent discount into effect under the terms of the Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement and the Memory Care Residency Agreement.

**Article 6. Termination for cause.** Larkspur may terminate for cause only after the plan's for-cause notice period of written notice from the executive director; the desk never initiates or reverses such a termination.

**Article 7. Change of apartment.** A resident may change apartments on the campus under the same agreement: a larger apartment type requires payment of the difference between the entrance fees of the two types at current prices under the same plan where the plan makes the upsize difference due; a smaller type refunds nothing where the plan refunds no downsize difference; and the plan's apartment change fee is charged on the independent living account.

**Article 8. Status.** Notices and apartment changes may be recorded only while the agreement is in occupied status.

## Notice period boundary (hypothetical, a 90 day period)

| Notice signed (day 0) | Day termination is recorded | Day number | Recording permitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 29 May | 89 | No |
| 1 March | 30 May | 90 | Yes, the termination date |

## Who may sign a notice or a withdrawal

| Signer | Accepted |
|---|---|
| The resident | Yes |
| Representative recorded with financial power of attorney, durable power of attorney or guardianship | Yes |
| Any other caller | No |

## Upsize difference (hypothetical prices under one plan)
A move from a type priced today at 340900.00 to a type priced today at 405900.00 under the same plan makes 65000.00 due, the difference at current prices; the reverse move refunds nothing.
